citation: Kruyt J., de Jong N.H., D'Ausilio A., Beňuš Š. (2023). Measuring prosodic entrainment in conversation: a review and comparison of different methods. JSLHR 66(11):4280-4314.
verification_level: ABSTRACT (full text restricted; method list not verified)
research_question: Do different entrainment methods agree when applied to the same data?
method: 12 methods on one corpus: global/local proximity, convergence, synchrony, time-series methods, LMM prediction
main_findings: Methods give differing results; each may capture a different type of entrainment
uncertainty_and_limitations: Single corpus; three F0 features; detail beyond abstract unverified
what_remains_unanswered: No method is a conditional, forward-predictive, speaker-disjoint increment; magnitudes not comparable to block partial R2

citation: Wynn C.J., Borrie S.A. (2022). Classifying conversational entrainment of speech behavior: an expanded framework and review. Journal of Phonetics 94:101173.
research_question: How should entrainment types and measures be classified?
method: narrative review and framework
main_findings: Terminology and measurement vary widely; some approaches fit no existing framework
what_remains_unanswered: Framework, not evidence on the predictive question

citation: Levitan R., Hirschberg J. (2011). Measuring acoustic-prosodic entrainment with respect to multiple levels and dimensions. Interspeech 2011, 3081-3084.
research_question: Do speakers entrain globally and turn-by-turn in intensity, pitch, rate and voice quality?
population_and_dataset: Columbia Games Corpus; cooperative computer games; partners separated by a curtain; Standard American English
prosodic_features_and_definitions: mean/max intensity, mean/max pitch, jitter, shimmer, NHR, speaking rate; final IPU vs initial IPU of next turn; z-scored by GENDER, not by speaker
method: paired t-tests (partner vs non-partner distance); Pearson correlation of adjacent IPUs (synchrony); 10-shuffle permutation check
main_findings: Turn-level proximity in every dimension; synchrony r = 0.47-0.50 (intensity), 0.28 (mean pitch), 0.15 (speaking rate)
uncertainty_and_limitations: 12 sessions; gender rather than speaker normalisation, so r includes between-speaker and session variance; turns treated as independent
coda_question_informed: H1 magnitude prior; H4; feature set
what_remains_unanswered: Spec §5/§8.1 cites this paper for per-speaker z-scoring; the paper z-scores by gender. Unconditioned r is an upper bound on CODA's conditional increment

citation: Levitan R., Gravano A., Hirschberg J. (2011). Entrainment in speech preceding backchannels. ACL-HLT 2011 (short), 113-117.
research_question: Do partners entrain on backchannel-preceding cues?
method: similarity of cue sets over time; relation to task success
main_findings: Partners entrain on backchannel-preceding cues; similarity grows and relates to coordination and task success
what_remains_unanswered: Not reply-delivery prediction; no lexical conditioning

citation: Heldner M., Edlund J., Hirschberg J. (2010). Pitch similarity in the vicinity of backchannels. Interspeech 2010, 3054-3057.
research_question: Is backchannel pitch closer to the preceding interlocutor utterance than non-backchannel pitch?
population_and_dataset: Columbia Games Corpus, close-talking microphones, separate channels
prosodic_features_and_definitions: pitch of responses vs preceding interlocutor speech
method: inter-speaker pitch similarity by response category
main_findings: Backchannels are more similar in pitch to the immediately preceding utterance than non-backchannels
uncertainty_and_limitations: Results not read in full; one small corpus
what_remains_unanswered: Function-dependent LOCAL similarity already documented for backchannels; not as a conditional predictive increment

citation: Edlund J., Heldner M., Hirschberg J. (2009). Pause and gap length in face-to-face interaction. Interspeech 2009.
research_question: Do pause and gap durations co-vary dynamically between speakers?
method: dynamic convergence and synchrony

what_remains_unanswered: Timing co-variation, not reply-delivery prediction

citation: Gravano A., Beňuš Š., Levitan R., Hirschberg J. (2015). Backward mimicry and forward influence in prosodic contour choice in Standard American English. Interspeech 2015, 1839-1843.
research_question: Is contour entrainment directional?
method: directional entrainment measures; correlation with social variables
main_findings: Separating backward mimicry from forward influence clarifies links with engagement
what_remains_unanswered: Directionality studied for categorical contours, not continuous delivery increments

citation: Weise A., Levitan S.I., Hirschberg J., Levitan R. (2019). Individual differences in acoustic-prosodic entrainment in spoken dialogue. Speech Communication 115:78-87.
research_question: How much do individuals differ in local entrainment?
population_and_dataset: Deception corpus (interviewer/interviewee; native English and native Mandarin speakers of English) and a second corpus
prosodic_features_and_definitions: intensity, pitch, rate, jitter, shimmer, NHR; z-scored PER SPEAKER
method: per-speaker Pearson convergence and synchrony; permutation check
main_findings: Large individual variation in strength and direction; synchrony mostly positive; no gender or L1 effect
what_remains_unanswered: A correct citation for per-speaker z-scoring; individual variation means a pooled linear increment averages over heterogeneous coupling

citation: Weise A., Levitan R. (2018). Looking for structure in lexical and acoustic-prosodic entrainment behaviors. NAACL-HLT 2018 (short), 297-302.
research_question: Do entrainment measures share structure across features and levels?
method: correlation, clustering, PCA of entrainment measures
main_findings: No meaningful correlations, clusters or components among entrainment measures (a null result)
what_remains_unanswered: Weak prior for coupling organised in a few shared directions

citation: Ostrand R., Chodroff E. (2021). It's alignment all the way down, but not all the way up: speakers align on some features but not others within a dialogue. Journal of Phonetics 88:101074.

prosodic_features_and_definitions: spectral, temporal and syntactic features; holistic acoustic profile

main_findings: Alignment on temporal features and holistic profile, not on several spectral or syntactic features
what_remains_unanswered: Does not address conditional prediction

main_findings: Entrainment differs by dialog act; in cooperative games high-authority, frequent acts entrain most
uncertainty_and_limitations: Very small sample; global, same-act design
what_remains_unanswered: Function dependence documented globally for same-act pairs; not for adjacent call-response pairs, not predictive, not lexically conditioned

main_findings: NED separates real from shuffled sessions with 98.9% accuracy on Fisher
uncertainty_and_limitations: Session shuffling destroys all within-session temporal dependence, not only adjacency
what_remains_unanswered: Forward cross-turn prediction exists, but as a learned similarity without lexical conditioning, matched-capacity nulls or an effect size

citation: Cohen Priva U., Edelist L., Gleason E. (2017). Converging to the baseline: corpus evidence for convergence in speech rate to interlocutor's baseline. JASA 141(5):2989-2996.
doi_or_url: bibliographic record via https://vivo.brown.edu/display/ucohenpr (DOI not resolved)

research_question: Do speakers converge to the interlocutor's baseline rate estimated from other conversations?
prosodic_features_and_definitions: lexically normalised speech rate (observed vs expected word durations)

lexical_contextual_controls: rate normalised by expected word durations (a lexical control for rate)
main_findings: Own baseline dominates (standardised beta ~0.78); interlocutor baseline beta ~0.05 (E17)

citation: Fuscone S., Favre B., Prévot L. (2020). Neural representations of dialogical history for improving upcoming turn acoustic parameters prediction. Interspeech 2020, 4203-4207.
research_question: Does adding the interlocutor's previous turns to the upcoming speaker's history improve prediction of the upcoming turn's energy, F0 range and speech rate?
prosodic_features_and_definitions: turn mean energy (normalised by the speaker's conversation mean), F0 range (max-min), speech rate; inputs also duration and a 3-class dialog act
method: LSTM over N = 1-10 previous turns; speaker-only (S) vs speaker + interlocutor (S+I); linear baseline; hyperparameters searched per target and setup
evaluation_design: 10-fold with paired t-tests; split unit not stated
lexical_contextual_controls: dialog-act class and duration only; reply and partner words not conditioned
main_findings: S+I lowers L1 loss vs S for energy (N=1: 0.381 vs 0.416, p < 1e-8) and F0 range (0.371 vs 0.390, p < 0.05); no gain for speech rate
uncertainty_and_limitations: Energy normalised by a conversation mean that includes the target turn; capacity not matched; no pairing-destroying null; no effect size or MDE
coda_question_informed: H1 (closest prior work); H4 (recency); capacity argument
what_remains_unanswered: Closest prior study, absent from the existing survey. Open: reply-word and partner-transcript conditioning, speaker-disjoint evaluation, matched-capacity nulls, block effect sizes with an MDE
